title: Your share doubled. Did you make money?

scenes.head: Your share doubled. Did you make money?
scenes.body: It depends which money you count in.
scenes.line: Eh, have a seat and let's have our money talk, quickly. Your share price doubled. Congratulations! But did you really make money? It depends on which money you are counting in.
scenes.img: A happy young Nigerian woman celebrating while looking at her phone, confetti-like golden light, living room

scenes.head: In naira: you doubled
scenes.line: Say you put 1 million Naira into a share, and some years later it is worth 2 million Naira. In naira, you doubled your money.
scenes.img: Two neat stacks of Nigerian naira notes on a desk, one twice as tall as the other, warm light

scenes.head: In dollars: maybe not
scenes.body: If the naira lost half its value, your dollars stayed the same.
scenes.line: Now look closely. If, over the same years, the naira lost half its value against the dollar, your 2 million Naira buys the same dollars your 1 million did before. In dollars, you stood still.
scenes.img: Naira notes and US dollar notes side by side on a table with a calculator, close-up, moody light

scenes.head: And Mr. Inflation is waiting
scenes.body: Rising prices eat into the gain too.
scenes.line: And Mr. Inflation is also waiting. If prices in the market doubled too, your 2 million Naira only buys the same things your 1 million used to buy.
scenes.img: A busy Nigerian open-air food market with a woman frowning at prices, baskets of tomatoes and peppers

scenes.head: Check your real return
scenes.body: Compare with inflation, and with the dollar if you think in dollars.
scenes.line: So, what should you check? Compare your return with inflation. And if you live abroad or think in dollars, compare it with the exchange rate too. That is your real return.
scenes.img: A Nigerian man in the diaspora on a video call with family, laptop on a desk, cosy flat, evening

scenes.head: Real growth beats rising prices
scenes.body: Anything less, and you're running on the spot.
scenes.line: The goal is simple. Growth that beats rising prices is real growth. Anything less, and you are running on the spot.
scenes.img: A Nigerian woman jogging at sunrise along the Lagos lagoon, golden light, energetic

scenes.head: Know the stock before you buy the story.
scenes.body: One plain-English money lesson every weekday at moloneystreetre.com
